statement: The maximum number of real smooth plane quartics through thirteen general real points and tangent to one general real line is six.

answer.text: With one line tangency, the maximum is 6 and total reality is attained.

source.location: Section 4, Theorem; complex upper count in Section 2, specialized to degree 4
source.version: Published article (2000), printed pp.176–177,183–184; primary PDF checked 9 November 2026

scope: Smooth irreducible degree-4 plane curves through thirteen general real points and tangent to one general real line.
notes: The total-reality construction is the degree-four specialization of the theorem in Section 4. The complex count is 2(d−1)=6. This record was separated from the two-tangency Bertrand result.
